description: Synthetic evaluation passages derived from owner-approved corpus definitions. These are controls, not newly discovered research findings or pinned quotations. Expected verdicts are evaluation-only and excluded from model requests.

excerpts.text: The sharp response is max(q,0). It is zero for q<=0 and proportional to the excess for q>0.
The other response is q*(1+tanh(q/epsilon))/2, epsilon>0. It has an explicitly intended negative tail for q<0.
For v in R^n, the gradient norm |v| is not differentiable at v=0.
We apply a smooth scalar tanh switch to a signed excess involving |v|; no cancellation or gradient regularization is supplied.
Four node positions have Y coordinates (3,3,3,3), so the reference residual at this state is zero. No evolution rule is specified.
Reciprocal scaling by lambda and 1/lambda, lambda>0, preserves the scalar product SR. No time-evolution law is specified.
Let the permitted region be [-1,1] and the available actions be A={0}. Its boundary is {-1,1}.
A boundary-margin model measures unsigned distance to that boundary; an outside action at 2 has distance 1.
Socio-Didact is a coined situational observation and learning mode. It need not be dominant, strategic, or unusually intelligent.
Sens means personal intent; Sin means socially constrained or encoded expression in this corpus. The writer preserves Sens while adjusting Sin.
The optional response a(q)=0 for q<=0 and q*exp[-(epsilon/q)^2] for q>0, epsilon>0, is C-infinity in q. Global PDE regularity is not proved here.

sources.provenance: Synthetic summary of the checked derivation at https://github.com/NousVolition/My-Sources-Project-ALL/blob/2d99c8c4fe36f4ca1e8b25339ab0358211bffbd3/math/notes/smooth-initial-field.tex; not a verbatim source quotation.

excerpts.text: The stated Cartesian initial field is proved smooth, divergence-free throughout R^3, rapidly decreasing, and finite-energy for R>=0, a,b>0 and finite real A,B. The derivation follows. Global smooth evolution is not proved here; no singularity theorem is asserted. This initial-data construction does not establish periodic-box compatibility or a theorem for modified forcing.

Here q=x^2+y^2 is squared radial position. Define phi=exp[-(q-R^2)^2/a^4-z^2/b^2], H=1-2*z^2/b^2, C=2-4*q*(q-R^2)/a^4, and u0=(-A*x*H-B*y,-A*y*H+B*x,A*z*C)*phi. The Cartesian formula has no division by the radial coordinate.

Differentiating gives partial_x(u0_x)+partial_y(u0_y)=-A*H*C*phi and partial_z(u0_z)=+A*H*C*phi: the sum is exactly zero, including on the axis. Components and derivatives are polynomials times phi. The bound (q-R^2)^2>=q^2/2-R^4 gives rapid decay, proving the field is Schwartz with finite energy. Finite implementation tests support the code; the analytic derivation establishes these initial-field properties.
